column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
Why does someone who badly wants a phone but cannot afford it not count as demand in the economist's sense?
Srivalli bought 1 kg of mangoes at Rs 150, 2 kg at Rs 100 and 3 kg at Rs 50. What rule does this show and what shape does it give on a graph?
How do you get the demand of a whole market from the demand of single customers, and why does the market curve respond more to price changes?
If coffee gets expensive, what happens to tea, and if more printers are sold, what happens to cartridges?
Why would you buy fewer and fewer mangoes at the same price as you eat more, and why might people delay buying a TV just before a festival?
Why do sellers bring more mangoes to market when the price is high, and what shape does that give on a graph?
Why are mangoes dearer at the start of the season than in the middle, and how do you build market supply from individual sellers?
Why might a farmer change crops when the price of one falls, and what happens to price when many new sellers enter a market?
How can new technology and expectations about next season's demand change how much farmers bring to market?
If mangoes are priced very low, what happens to buyers and sellers, and what happens if they are priced very high?
At what point does a market have neither a shortage nor a surplus, and what happens to the price there?
Why can no real market stay at one equilibrium price forever?
What happened to mask prices at the start and later in the pandemic, and why do hotel room rates differ between July and New Year's Eve?
What do a maximum price on medicines and a legal lower limit on pay have in common, and why is a market with one dominant seller a problem for buyers?
Why is a neighbourhood park unlikely to be built if every family waits for the others to pay for it, and who steps in?
Why might a farmer grow less wheat if the government sets its price below what the market would pay?
How can too many permits discourage someone from starting a small restaurant, and how can price controls discourage investment in better seeds?
